conditions: For arbitrary positive integers $d_x,d_y$, let $f(x,y)=x_1$. This function is $C^\infty$ on the whole space and satisfies the stated $C^2$ assumptions. The model imposes no lower boundedness, compact primal domain, strong concavity, or existence promise. For any candidate $(x^\star,y^\star)$, any $r_0>0$, and any admissible $h$, choose $0<r\le r_0$ and $x=x^\star-(r/2)e_1$. For every $y^\prime$, $f(x,y^\prime)=x_1^\star-r/2<f(x^\star,y^\star)$, violating the second inequality in the local minimax definition. Thus an instance without a solution exists in every allowed dimension; even revealing the entire function cannot produce a valid output. The notation $N^\star=+\infty$ uses the convention that the successful-algorithm class is empty. The explanatory status is `infeasible_task`.
applicability.dimension_conditions: Any $d_x,d_y\ge1$ are allowed. The counterexample already holds at $d_x=d_y=1$.
applicability.oracle_mapping: The counterexample is independent of the information available. Exact-value and gradient interfaces satisfy the model, and additional information cannot create a nonexistent point.
applicability.guarantee_mapping: The requirement that one algorithm succeed on every instance fails because the class contains an admissible instance with no solution.
applicability.resource_mapping: No algorithm succeeds, so neither a finite nor an infinite query budget satisfies the task on the entire class.

bounds.hidden_constants: This no-solution counterexample involves no asymptotic constant or accuracy threshold.
bounds.lower_scope_type_note: An admissible instance has an empty solution set, so no output strategy can succeed. No span, zero-respecting, or queried-output restriction is needed.
